issues.issue: PRI may elect, "at its sole discretion", between a penny-rate royalty tied to an "equivalent Record not in the form of a compact disc" and a percentage of the compact disc Royalty Base; neither "equivalent Record" nor "other new Record configuration" is defined. Which configurations are captured, and what the equivalent is, is left open.

The parties are to "negotiate in good faith regarding an adjustment" of the compact disc royalty "taking into account industry-wide standards" — an agreement to agree with no fallback beyond continuing 7.04(a). What good faith requires here has no ascertainable content.

"Premium Records, Budget Records, or Records other than Albums not otherwise specifically referred to herein" is a residual catch-all set against enumerated categories, and it is unclear whether the qualifier "not otherwise specifically referred to herein" modifies all three items or only the last. Whether a given configuration falls into this half-rate bucket rather than a specific rate turns on that reading.

This residual half-rate provision overlaps with paragraph 7.02(a)'s full album rate and paragraph 7.06(a)'s 50%-of-net-receipts rate, and the agreement supplies no priority rule for a Record that answers to more than one of them. Which royalty governs a novel configuration is not resolved by the instrument as a whole.

The denominator is "the Royalty Base applicable to PRI's or its licensees' top-line single-disc LPs", an undefined and moving benchmark that neither party can fix in advance. The multiple-record royalty cannot be computed without construing it.

The 50%-of-net-receipts categories are enumerated but end with open-ended language — "licenses of Master Recordings on a flat-fee basis" and distribution "by any combination of the methods set forth above or other methods" — so the reach of the catch-all against the listed specifics is genuinely uncertain. Whether a particular exploitation (notably licensed digital distribution) falls inside this paragraph is exactly what the words leave open.

This paragraph cannot be reconciled with paragraph 7.02(a), which pays 11% of the Royalty Base for Albums sold through Normal Retail Channels; one and the same exploitation can be described as a licence under 7.06(a) and a sale under 7.02(a), and no provision states which prevails. That conflict determines the royalty rate.

"Net receipts" is defined after deduction of amounts PRI must pay third parties "such as, without limitation, production costs ... mechanical copyright payments, AFofM and other union or guild payments" — an open-ended deduction catch-all against enumerated examples. What else PRI may deduct is unbounded.

The proviso caps non-royalty-bearing club Records at "fifty percent (50%) of the Records distributed hereunder through such clubs", but does not say what royalty applies once the cap is exceeded, and "cumulative basis" is left unexplained. The remedy for breach of the cap is unstated.

This affiliated-licensee direct-marketing rate of 5% overlaps with paragraph 7.06(a)(ii), which pays 50% of net receipts for the same distribution methods when licensed to Non-Affiliated Third Parties; whether a particular licensee is "affiliated" is nowhere defined. The dividing line between the two rates is left to construction.

PRI may hold "reasonable reserves" subject to percentage caps and a liquidation schedule, but "reasonable" is not defined and PRI may adopt "such other accounting periods as PRI may in general adopt". Both the size of reserves and the accounting cycle are left to one party's judgment.

Statements become "binding" and unobjectionable after three years, yet paragraph 8.05(a) allows suit within four years of the statement, so a claim can be timely under 8.05(a) while already barred under 8.03(a). The two limitation regimes cannot be fully harmonised.

Statements are deemed "conclusively" rendered on the 8.01 due date unless Grantor objects within thirty days, which starts the three-year clock in 8.03(a) and the four-year clock in 8.05(a) from a date on which no statement may in fact have been sent. Its interaction with those two limitation provisions is not worked out.

The audit right covers "the six (6) accounting periods prior to such audit" but may be exercised "only within three (3) years after the date when PRI is required to send" the statement; six semi-annual periods is three years, so the two limits may or may not coincide depending on when the audit begins. The audit window is not clearly fixed.

The four-year contractual limitations period runs "from the date such statement of accounting for royalties or such payment was rendered", which does not say what happens where several statements or payments relate to the same royalties. The accrual date for a continuing under-accounting is left open.

The four-year suit period cannot be squared with paragraph 8.03(a), under which statements become binding and immune from objection after three years; a suit brought in year four would concern a statement Grantor is deemed to have approved. Which period controls is a genuine internal inconsistency.

The limitation is disapplied "in the event any court determines fraud or gross negligence on the part of PRI", yet the same clause purports to deny the court "authority to consider any other issues" — so the court can only find fraud by first exceeding the authority the clause allows it. That circularity leaves the carve-out's operation unclear.

The rate is the "Statutory Rate prevailing at the time of release in the applicable country", but the provision covers both the United States and Canada, which have different statutory regimes, and "Statutory Rate" is not defined in this Article. The applicable rate must be construed.

Copyright royalties are payable on 50% of "Album free goods, as defined in paragraph 13.15(a)(ii) below" but not on Albums "distributed pursuant to special sales plans", a phrase left undefined and standing against the defined free-goods category. The line between the two distributions is not drawn.

Public-domain arrangements are royalty-free unless the arranged version "varies substantially from the original work", an undefined threshold that determines whether any mechanical royalty is owed. The test invites competing readings.

The provision breaks off mid-sentence at "Mechanical royalty reserves maintained by PRI against anticipated returns", so the liquidation rule for those reserves is missing from the text. The incomplete sentence leaves the reserve mechanic unstated.

The 30%/40% mechanical reserve caps mirror the record-royalty reserve caps in paragraph 8.01 but come with no liquidation schedule of the kind 8.01 prescribes, so it is unclear whether 8.01's liquidation timetable applies to mechanical reserves. The two reserve regimes do not fit together.
